title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the customer-success and support guidance we use for enterprise customers during onboarding, integration, ongoing support, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs). The document covers: onboarding checklist, integration guide highlights, escalation matrix and procedures, common known issues and workarounds, health check metrics and QBR templates. Use this as the canonical reference for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), and Support Engineers.

1) Quick intro and goals

- Goal: get enterprise customers live on Redwood Inference with validated performance, security posture, and an agreed support/engagement cadence within 8 weeks for standard integrations.
- Success criteria: production calls allowed, SSO and KMS integrated (if required), performance baselines validated (latency & throughput), acceptance sign-off from customer.

2) Roles & ownership

- CSM: primary customer relationship, QBR owner, coordinates internal teams.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): integration lead, initial architecture review, runbook author.
- Support Engineer: triage and resolve incidents; first contact for P1/P2.
- Technical Account Manager (TAM, if assigned): ongoing technical liaison and roadmap coordination.
- Eng-on-call: used for escalations beyond Support Engineer's remit (performance regressions, runtime bugs).

3) Onboarding checklist (recommended 8-week cadence)

Phase A — Kickoff (week 0)
- Deliverables: kickoff meeting, success criteria, communication plan, contacts list, shared workspace created (Slack channel / email thread).
- Action items: collect network/egress requirements, SSO/SAML details, KMS/HSM requirements, compliance controls required (SOC2/ISO).

Phase B — Architecture & Integration (weeks 1-3)
- Deliverables: integration plan, VPC/peering design (if Private), API key provisioning plan, security review.
- Action items: test API calls to sandbox, validate model selection for workload, configure rate limits and quotas.
- Integration checklist (SE):
  1. Confirm API base URL and auth method (API key, OAuth, or mTLS).
  2. Validate CORS/webhook behavior for browser-based inference.
  3. If Private deployment: confirm control plane access, routing, and firewall rules.
  4. For Dedicated: verify reserved capacity windows and autoscale policy.

Phase C — Performance Validation (weeks 3-5)
- Deliverables: throughput/latency baseline report, token-cost projection, regression test plan.
- Action items: run 3 representative workloads (chat, completion, embeddings), measure p50/p95/p99 latency and per-token cost.
- Acceptance thresholds (example): p95 latency < 800 ms for 1-2k tokens; error rate < 0.5% over 1 hour sustained. Adjust per customer SLA.

Phase D — Security & Compliance (weeks 4-6)
- Deliverables: evidence of logging/audit, KMS integration, data handling agreement signed.
- Action items: provide sample audit logs, confirm retention policy, verify RBAC and SSO.

Phase E — Launch & Handover (weeks 6-8)
- Deliverables: production keys, runbook handover, escalation contacts, first 30/60/90-day health-check calendar.
- Action items: schedule 30-day QBR, enable monitoring dashboards and alerts, ensure runbooks are in eng-sre/ and eng-platform as appropriate.

4) Integration guide highlights (quick reference)

- Auth patterns supported: API keys (default), OAuth2 for partner integrations, mTLS for private deployments.
- Suggested client SDK flow for server-side apps: 1) store API key in customer KMS; 2) call Redwood API via service account; 3) use streaming endpoints for low-latency UIs.

Example curl test (sandbox):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_API_KEY}\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b", "input":"Say hello" }'

Webhook config example (for async job updates):
| Field | Value | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| url | https://customer.example/webhooks/redwood | HTTPS endpoint with valid cert |
| secret | <HMAC secret> | Use to verify payloads |
| events | job.completed, job.failed | Subscribe only to required events |

- Network notes: allow outbound to our regional inference endpoints and to S3 endpoints for model artifacts. For Private deployments ensure the customer firewall allows control-plane CIDR ranges (see eng-infra/runbooks for list).

5) Escalation matrix & procedure

Severity levels and times-to-acknowledge (SLA baseline for enterprise customers):
- P1 (system unavailable / major outage impacting many users): ack within 15 min, 24x7 pager escalations.
- P2 (significant degradation / partial outage): ack within 1 hour, business-hours support and escalation to on-call if unresolved in 2 hours.
- P3 (feature regression / degraded performance for a limited scope): ack within 4 business hours.
- P4 (general questions / enhancement requests): respond within 2 business days.

Escalation steps (use numbered checklist):
1. Support Engineer triages and documents: logs, request IDs, sample payloads, timestamps.
2. If suspected production bug or capacity issue, escalate to Eng-on-call with summary and links to dashboards.
3. If security-sensitive, notify Security team and apply restricted confidentiality flag; follow incident-response-security playbook.
4. CSM notifies customer of next steps and ETA within SLA windows.
5. Post-resolution: create incident summary and action items; schedule postmortem for P1/P2 incidents.

Contact directory (examples):
- Support team (primary): support+enterprise@redwood.example
- On-call (pager): use PagerDuty schedule -> \"redwood-inference-prod\"
- Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.example
- Escalation owner (CSM): see customer record in Salesforce (link in CSM dashboard).

6) Known issues & workarounds (operational table)

| Issue | Symptoms | Impact | Workaround / Mitigation | Owner |
|-------|----------|--------|--------------------------|-------|
| Intermittent streaming disconnections | SSE/WS disconnects after ~2 min | Affects long-running streams | 1) Retry logic with resume token; 2) Use chunked shorter sessions; 3) Check reverse proxy timeouts | Support/SE |
| Elevated latency during autoscale | p95 increases during burst traffic | Performance degradation for short windows | Pre-warm capacity, increase reserved Dedicated capacity, enable burst window | Eng-SRE/Platform |
| Incorrect role-based access errors on Private | 403 responses for some users | Access denied for certain APIs | Verify RBAC mappings and SSO group sync; perform manual sync if needed | Support/Customer Success |
| Missing audit logs for short window | Gaps seen in audit stream | Compliance risk | Confirm agent/collector health, fallback to local log cache, escalate to Eng-Infra | Security/Eng-Infra |

7) Support process & runbook links

- Triage checklist: collect request ID, timestamps, API key used (masked), model name, full request/response (redact PII), relevant logs, tracing links (per-route).
- Evidence required for escalation to Eng-on-call: reproducible test, perf profile (flame graph / p50/p95), and isolation steps.
- Runbook links: \"/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks\" (for capacity/incident), \"/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues\" (runtime bugs), \"/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security\" (security).

8) Health checks & QBR materials

Suggested periodic checks (30/60/90 day cadence):
- Usage & cost: total tokens, cost per 1k tokens, top routes by traffic.
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate (% of requests failing).
- Availability: uptime %, incident count last period.
- Quality: model hallucination/regression alerts, sample prompt set evaluation.
- Security & access: last successful SSO sync, KMS rotation date, audit log integrity.

QBR template (talking points for customer-facing review):
1. Executive summary (1 slide): health & top metrics.
2. Adoption metrics: active users, top endpoints, growth.
3. Performance & reliability: SLA attainment, incidents and remediations.
4. Cost economics: per-API call costs and optimization opportunities.
5. Roadmap alignment: upcoming runtime features and any customer-specific requests.
6. Action items & next steps: owners and target dates.

Example QBR checklist (CSM):
- Pull dashboards for last 90 days; export CSV for customer.
- Run the quality evaluation on canonical prompt set; include regression analysis.
- Confirm security posture and compliance artifacts are current.
- Prepare recommendations for cost/perf optimization (batching, model/quantization changes).

9) Postmortem & continuous improvement

- For P1/P2 incidents: write a public postmortem within 5 business days (redacted for customer-sensitive info), and an internal technical RCA in eng channels.
- Track recurring issues in the regression-triage board and prioritize fixes or workarounds in roadmap.

10) Templates & attachments (copyable assets)

- 30/60/90-day health check email template: [CSM copy available in templates folder].
- QBR slide deck template: location \"/confluence/customer-success-and-support/qbr-templates\".
- Sample runbook snippet (incident triage):
  1. Acknowledge ticket and set P-level. 2. Gather logs/traces. 3. Reproduce in sandbox. 4. Escalate if not resolvable in 60 minutes for P1.

11) Related references

- eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking (egress/CIDR lists)
- eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite (load testing scripts)
- security-and-compliance/incident-response-security (security incident playbooks)
